hypotheses.name: Out-of-frame deletions → truncated dystrophin → sarcolemmal fragility
hypotheses.subtitle: Monaco rule; loss of C-terminal DGC anchor; membrane tears → Ca²⁺ influx → necrosis
hypotheses.therapeutic: Exon-skipping ASOs (Dp427m rescue); micro-dystrophin gene therapy

detail.lede: Out-of-frame deletions in DMD ablate the C-terminal dystroglycan-binding domain, decoupling the sarcolemma from the extracellular matrix. Contraction stress produces membrane micro-tears, unregulated Ca²⁺ influx activates calpain and disrupts mitochondrial handling, triggering necrosis and progressive fibro-fatty replacement.

evidence.text: Monaco reading-frame rule: 90% of out-of-frame → DMD; 91% of in-frame → BMD
LOVD: 18,204 out-of-frame deletion entries vs 4,822 in-frame (matches 68% severe rate)
Dystrophin-null mdx muscle: elevated resting [Ca²⁺]ᵢ and calpain activation
Membrane sealants (poloxamer-188) reduce sarcolemmal damage in mdx / GRMD
Micro-dystrophin (rAAV) restores DGC + delays fibrosis in Phase III
Exon-51 skipping (eteplirsen) restores in-frame Dp427m in ~13% of pts
Frame-rule exception: Δexon 5 in-frame → severe DMD via aberrant splicing
Contraction-induced micro-tears in mdx sarcolemma admit extracellular Ca²⁺ down its steep gradient.
Calpain-1 is activated by elevated cytosolic [Ca²⁺] and proteolyses a broad set of sarcomeric + membrane substrates.
Sustained Ca²⁺ overload opens the mitochondrial permeability transition pore, collapsing ΔΨₘ and triggering ROS.
Mdx mitochondria show reduced membrane potential and elevated superoxide output under contractile load.
Cyclophilin-D knockout (blocks MPTP opening) rescues necrosis in mdx muscle.
Elevated serum creatine kinase is a clinical proxy for ongoing sarcolemmal permeability + necrosis in DMD.
Serial injury cycles deplete the satellite-cell pool via replicative senescence.
Mdx satellite cells show telomere shortening and impaired self-renewal by late disease.
Fibro-adipogenic progenitors expand and differentiate when muscle regeneration fails, replacing myofibers with fat + collagen.
TGF-β signalling drives fibrotic ECM deposition in DMD muscle biopsies.
Frameshift produced by exon deletion introduces a PTC downstream, on average within ~200 codons.
Reading-frame rule: deletion produces a PTC unless total deleted length ≡ 0 mod 3.
Nonsense-mediated decay degrades transcripts with a PTC ≥50 nt upstream of the last exon-exon junction.
Western blot of DMD muscle: <3% dystrophin detected in PTC-carrying patients.
Dystrophin C-terminal domain binds β-dystroglycan, bridging cytoskeletal actin to sarcolemmal laminin via the DGC.
In dystrophin-null mdx muscle, DGC components (β-DG, sarcoglycans, nNOS) dissociate from the sarcolemma.

therapeutic.label1: Therapeutic entry: exon skipping · micro-dystrophin AAV
therapeutic.label2: restores in-frame Dp427m or delivers truncated functional protein

hypotheses.name: In-frame deletions → partial-function dystrophin → BMD phenotype
hypotheses.subtitle: Central-rod deletion retains N-term + DGC; slower progression, later onset
hypotheses.therapeutic: Small-molecule stabilizers (utrophin upregulation); guides ASO target selection

detail.lede: In-frame deletions in the central rod domain remove spectrin-like repeats but preserve the N-terminal actin-binding domain and the C-terminal DGC anchor. A shortened but functional dystrophin still couples the sarcolemma to the ECM, yielding reduced but non-zero membrane stability — the biological basis of BMD's later onset and slower progression.

evidence.text: Monaco reading-frame rule: 91% of in-frame deletions → BMD phenotype
Δexons 45–47 (in-frame, spectrin repeats 17-19) → BMD with ambulation to 40s+
Truncated dystrophin visualized on Western in BMD muscle at ~50–80% wild-type levels
Micro-dystrophin (Δrod) rescue in mdx approximates the BMD state
Some large in-frame deletions (Δexons 3–41) still produce severe DMD — position matters
Partial DGC bears mechanical load but with reduced fidelity — subclinical membrane injury still occurs.
Low-grade Ca²⁺ leak produces slower calpain activation and delayed cellular damage.
BMD muscle biopsies show necrosis foci at lower density than DMD — regeneration keeps pace longer.
BMD patients often retain ambulation into their 30s–40s; cardiomyopathy still develops but later.
The clinical BMD label is applied when ambulation is retained past age 16.
In-frame indels remove spectrin repeats without shifting the reading frame; typical central-rod deletions span exons 45–55.
Shortened dystrophin retains the N-terminal actin-binding domain and the C-terminal β-DG binding domain.
DGC assembles around a partial dystrophin; sarcoglycans + β-DG remain at the sarcolemma at reduced levels.

therapeutic.label1: Therapeutic entry: utrophin upregulation · exon-skipping toward in-frame
therapeutic.label2: convert DMD reading-frame to a BMD-like partial rescue

hypotheses.name: Nonsense / splice variants → NMD → tissue-graded transcript loss
hypotheses.subtitle: Premature stop triggers surveillance; cardiac + brain isoforms less rescued
hypotheses.therapeutic: Readthrough agents (ataluren); NMD inhibitors under investigation

detail.lede: Nonsense mutations and canonical splice-site variants create a premature termination codon (PTC). Transcripts with a PTC ≥50 nt upstream of the last exon-exon junction are degraded by nonsense-mediated decay (NMD), yielding near-total dystrophin loss. NMD efficiency varies across tissues, so cardiac and brain-restricted isoforms sometimes retain trace expression — a tissue-graded loss pattern.

evidence.text: PTC ≥50 nt upstream of last EEJ triggers NMD in mammalian cells
Nonsense-variant DMD muscle: <3% dystrophin by Western blot
Ataluren (Translarna) promotes ribosomal readthrough of PTC codons → partial rescue
Splice-site variants generate downstream PTC in ~70% of cases (via exon skipping or intron retention)
NMD efficiency varies 2–5× across tissues; brain + cardiac often show partial escape
NMD activity varies by tissue and transcript context; brain isoforms show partial NMD escape.
PTC codons in favorable sequence contexts are susceptible to pharmacological readthrough (aminoglycosides, ataluren).
Muscle NMD is efficient → near-total Dp427m loss → severe DMD phenotype indistinguishable from deletion carriers.
Cardiac + CNS symptoms track residual isoform expression; partial NMD escape can soften those phenotypes.
Ataluren approval (EMA 2014) requires a nonsense mutation genotype; ~13% of DMD patients are eligible.
Nonsense codons directly encode a PTC; splice-site variants produce a PTC via exon skipping or intron retention.
The exon-junction complex marks a PTC as NMD-eligible when it lies ≥50 nt upstream of the terminal EEJ.
NMD reduces mutant mRNA levels to ~5-15% of wild-type in patient muscle biopsies.

therapeutic.label1: Therapeutic entry: ataluren readthrough · NMD-inhibitor combinations
therapeutic.label2: restore partial protein production from PTC-containing mRNA

hypotheses.name: Distal-promoter variants → tissue-specific isoform loss (Dp140/Dp71)
hypotheses.subtitle: 5′-restricted lesions spare muscle but ablate CNS/retinal isoforms — cognitive/ERG phenotype

detail.lede: Variants in the 3′ half of DMD (exons 45–79) or in the internal promoters of Dp140, Dp116, and Dp71 selectively ablate the shorter isoforms while sparing Dp427m in skeletal and cardiac muscle. Patients with these variants often present with cognitive impairment, retinal ERG abnormalities, or kidney phenotypes, but with preserved motor function — an isoform-scoped disease pattern distinct from classical DMD.

evidence.text: Dp71 knockout in mice: ubiquitous but subtle phenotypes (retinal ERG, kidney podocyte)
DMD patients with distal deletions have lower IQ, correlated with Dp140 loss
Dp260 (retinal) loss → negative ERG b-wave — a clinical marker of DMD
Dp116 loss in Schwann cells → subtle peripheral nerve conduction changes
Cohort is small (n=612 in LOVD) — statistical power for isoform-phenotype mapping is limited
Patients with variants ablating Dp140 show cognitive IQ deficits averaging ~10 points below patients with Dp140-sparing variants.
Retinal loss of Dp260 produces a negative-configuration b-wave on scotopic ERG — a clinical marker of DMD retinal involvement.
Distal variants (exon ≥45) fall downstream of Dp427m's transcribed region only when they lie in later exons; Dp427m's promoter and full-length mRNA remain intact.
Dp140's promoter is in intron 44; Dp71's promoter is in intron 62. Variants distal to these ablate specific isoforms.
Dp427m preserved → sarcolemmal DGC intact → skeletal + cardiac muscle spared from progressive dystrophy.
Dp140 is the dominant dystrophin isoform in cortical astrocytes; Dp71 supports ubiquitous CNS expression.
Dp260 is the retina-specific isoform; Dp71 provides retinal backup expression.
Dp71 is expressed in podocytes and glomerular capillaries; loss correlates with albuminuria in mdx variants.

therapeutic.label2: deliver Dp140/Dp71 mini-genes under tissue-restricted promoters

rules.notes: Approximation of Popp & Maquat 2013: PTCs upstream of the last exon-exon junction trigger NMD; late PTCs escape. Splice-site variants are assumed to trigger NMD via exon skipping. In-frame and missense variants are 'transcript-dependent' — no PTC generated.
